# Install AI-Forward into a local repository

Use this skill when a project does not yet have the AI-Forward Pack and you want the first install to respect the repository that already exists. It reads the target before writing, applies the pack deployment map, and reports what landed.

## When to use it

Use `addpacktorepo` from an AI-Forward clone when you are onboarding another local Git repository for the first time. If the target already contains `docs/ai-forward-pack/INSTALL.md`, use [update an installed pack](#skill-updatepack) instead.

## What you need

You need the local path to the target repository and access to the pack source. The target must be a Git repository. Be ready to review any planned change to existing `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github`, `.claude`, `.grok`, `.agents` or `docs` files.

## Try it

Slash-command harnesses:

```text
/addpacktorepo C:\Projects\harbortasks
```

Codex equivalent:

```text
$addpacktorepo C:\Projects\harbortasks
```

Preview first if you want zero writes:

```text
/addpacktorepo dry run C:\Projects\harbortasks
```

## What happens

The skill inspects the target's language mix, existing agent instructions and docs. It uses the pack's deployment map rather than copying files by memory. Existing managed blocks are replaced wholesale; existing local content is not silently overwritten.

## What you get

Illustrative output shape:

```text
Area        Destination                         Status
skills      .claude/skills, .agents/skills      installed
copilot     .github/prompts, .github/agents     installed
docs        docs/ai-forward-pack                installed
explorer    docs/index.html                     skipped: already existed
```

The result is an installed pack surface and a summary table. It offers a commit and push; you decide.

## Review before continuing

Confirm that existing instructions were preserved, `docs/docs-index.js` was not seeded, language-specific rules were scoped correctly, and optional CI files were added only if you accepted them.

## Tips and recovery

If the install is interrupted, rerun it; the operation is designed to be idempotent. If the skill detects an existing install, stop and run [updatepack](#skill-updatepack). On Windows, run scripts as `python` or `py -3` when examples show `python3`.

## Where to go next

Run [adopt](#skill-adopt) to recover the existing repo into the knowledge graph, then use [specify](#skill-specify) for the next real feature.
